title: Wi-Fi connected but no internet
symptoms: connected to wifi but websites not opening
wifi shows connected no internet access
net not working though wifi is on
steps: Turn the router off, wait 30 seconds, and turn it on again.
Check whether other devices on the same Wi-Fi have internet.
Run 'ipconfig /release' then 'ipconfig /renew' in Command Prompt.
Flush DNS with 'ipconfig /flushdns'.
Change DNS to 8.8.8.8 and 8.8.4.4 in adapter settings.
If still failing, contact your ISP.

title: Slow Wi-Fi speed
steps: Run a speed test and compare with your plan speed.
Move closer to the router or remove obstacles.
Disconnect devices that are not in use.
Switch to the 5 GHz band if your router supports it.
Restart the router and your device.
Update the Wi-Fi adapter driver.

title: Cannot see Wi-Fi network in the list
steps: Make sure Airplane mode is off and Wi-Fi is switched on.
Check the physical Wi-Fi switch or Fn key on the laptop.
Restart the router and your device.
Open Device Manager and enable the Wi-Fi adapter.
Update or reinstall the Wi-Fi driver.
If the network is hidden, add it manually using the SSID.

title: Wi-Fi keeps disconnecting
steps: Forget the network and reconnect with the password.
Disable power saving for the Wi-Fi adapter in Device Manager.
Update the Wi-Fi driver.
Change the router channel to 1, 6 or 11.
Restart the router; update its firmware if possible.

title: Wi-Fi password incorrect error
symptoms: cannot connect incorrect network security key
steps: Re-enter the password carefully; it is case sensitive.
Check the password on the router label or ask the network admin.
Forget the network and connect again.
Restart the router and try again.

title: VPN not connecting
steps: Confirm your normal internet connection works.
Close and reopen the VPN client.
Check that your username and password are correct.
Try another VPN server or gateway if available.
Disable firewall or antivirus temporarily to test.
Reinstall the VPN client and retry.

title: VPN connected but cannot access office resources
symptoms: vpn connected but cannot open intranet
cannot access company server on vpn
vpn is on but shared drive not opening
internal website not loading over vpn
steps: Disconnect and reconnect the VPN.
Flush DNS with 'ipconfig /flushdns'.
Try the resource using its IP address instead of its name.
Check that your account has permission for that resource.
Raise a ticket so the network team can check VPN routing.

title: VPN very slow
steps: Test your internet speed without VPN.
Switch to a nearer VPN server.
Close bandwidth-heavy apps and downloads.
Use a wired connection if possible.
Switch the VPN protocol (for example UDP to TCP) in client settings.

title: VPN authentication failed
steps: Re-enter username and password; check Caps Lock.
If you use MFA, make sure the code is current.
Check that your system time is correct.
If your password changed recently, use the new password.
If still failing, raise a ticket; your account may be locked.

title: Printer not printing
steps: Check the printer is on and connected to the network or USB.
Make sure it is selected as the default printer.
Cancel all stuck jobs in the print queue.
Restart the Print Spooler service.
Restart the printer and the computer.
Reinstall the printer driver.

title: Printer offline status
steps: Turn the printer off and on.
Check network cable or Wi-Fi connection of the printer.
In Printers settings, untick 'Use Printer Offline'.
Remove and re-add the printer.
Restart the Print Spooler service.

title: Paper jam
steps: Switch off the printer and unplug it.
Open all covers and gently pull the paper in the direction of the paper path.
Check for torn pieces left inside.
Fan the paper stack and reload it properly.
Switch on and print a test page.

title: Poor print quality, faded or streaks
steps: Run the printer's head cleaning or maintenance utility.
Check ink or toner levels and replace if low.
Use the correct paper type in settings.
Print an alignment or test page.
If the problem continues, raise a ticket for hardware service.

title: Cannot add or find network printer
steps: Confirm you are on the office network or VPN.
Add the printer by IP address using 'Add a printer'.
Check the printer IP using its configuration page.
Install the correct driver from the manufacturer.
Ask the admin whether you have permission for that printer.

title: Forgot password
steps: Click 'Forgot password' on the login page.
Enter your registered email or employee ID.
Open the reset link or OTP sent to you.
Create a new password that follows the policy.
If you do not receive the mail, check spam or raise a ticket.

title: Account locked
symptoms: too many wrong attempts account locked
steps: Wait 15 to 30 minutes; many accounts unlock automatically.
Try the self-service unlock portal if your company has one.
Do not keep retrying with wrong passwords.
Raise a ticket so the admin can unlock the account.

title: Password expired
steps: Press Ctrl+Alt+Del and choose 'Change a password'.
Enter the old password and then the new password twice.
Use at least 8 characters with letters, numbers and symbols.
Do not reuse your recent passwords.
Update the saved password on your phone and email apps.

title: MFA or OTP not received
steps: Check mobile network signal and wait one minute.
Check that your phone date and time are set to automatic.
Request a new code; do not use an old one.
Use backup codes or another verification method.
If you changed your phone, raise a ticket to reset MFA.

title: Software installation fails
steps: Right-click the installer and choose 'Run as administrator'.
Check free disk space.
Temporarily disable antivirus and try again.
Download the installer again; the file may be corrupt.
Raise a ticket if you do not have install permissions.

title: Application crashing or not opening
steps: Close the app from Task Manager and open it again.
Restart the computer.
Update the application to the latest version.
Repair or reinstall the application.
Check Windows Update for pending fixes.

title: Microsoft Office activation problem
steps: Sign in to Office using your company account.
Check that your internet connection is working.
Go to File > Account > Update Options > Update Now.
Sign out and sign in again.
Raise a ticket if the licence is not assigned to you.

title: Outlook not opening or not syncing
steps: Check that you are online and not in Work Offline mode.
Close Outlook fully and reopen it.
Start Outlook in safe mode with 'outlook.exe /safe'.
Create a new Outlook profile in Control Panel > Mail.
Repair Office from Apps settings.

title: Browser slow or websites not loading
symptoms: pages take long to load in chrome
steps: Clear browser cache and cookies.
Disable unnecessary extensions.
Update the browser.
Try an incognito window to test.
Restart the computer and try another browser.

title: Windows update stuck or failing
steps: Wait at least an hour; some updates are slow.
Run the Windows Update Troubleshooter.
Free up at least 10 GB of disk space.
Restart the computer and try again.
Run 'sfc /scannow' in an administrator Command Prompt.

title: Laptop not turning on
steps: Check the charger and power outlet.
Remove the battery if possible, hold the power button for 30 seconds, then reconnect.
Try a different charger.
Disconnect all USB devices and try again.
If there is still no power, raise a ticket for hardware repair.

title: Laptop very slow or hanging
steps: Restart the computer.
Close unused programs and browser tabs.
Open Task Manager and check high CPU, memory or disk usage.
Disable unnecessary startup programs.
Free up disk space and run a malware scan.

title: Laptop overheating
symptoms: system shuts down due to heat
steps: Place the laptop on a hard, flat surface.
Close heavy applications.
Clean the vents with compressed air.
Use a cooling pad if possible.
Raise a ticket if the fan is not working.

title: Keyboard or mouse not working
steps: Restart the computer.
Try a different USB port or change the batteries for wireless devices.
Check that the touchpad is not disabled with the Fn key.
Update or reinstall the driver in Device Manager.
Test with another keyboard or mouse.

title: No display or external monitor not detected
steps: Check that the HDMI or display cable is firmly connected on both ends.
Press Windows + P and choose Extend or Duplicate.
Try a different cable or port.
Right-click the desktop > Display settings > Detect.
Update the graphics driver.

title: No sound from laptop
symptoms: volume is on but no sound
steps: Check that the volume is not muted.
Select the correct output device in sound settings.
Unplug and replug headphones.
Run the Windows audio troubleshooter.
Update or reinstall the audio driver.

title: USB device or pen drive not detected
steps: Try a different USB port.
Try the device on another computer.
Check Disk Management for the drive and assign a letter.
Update the USB drivers in Device Manager.
Note that company policy may block USB drives; check with IT.

title: Blue screen error
steps: Note the stop code shown on the screen.
Restart the computer.
Disconnect newly added devices.
Boot in Safe Mode and uninstall recently installed software or drivers.
Raise a ticket with the stop code if it repeats.

title: Low disk space
steps: Run Disk Cleanup and delete temporary files.
Empty the Recycle Bin and Downloads folder.
Uninstall programs you do not use.
Move large files to cloud or external storage.
Use Storage Sense in Windows settings.

title: Email not sending
steps: Check your internet connection.
Check the recipient's email address for typos.
Check that the attachment size is within the limit.
Remove the stuck mail from the Outbox and resend.
Restart the mail app and try again.

title: Mailbox full
symptoms: cannot receive new mails storage full
steps: Delete large emails and attachments.
Empty the Deleted Items and Junk folders.
Archive old emails.
Check 'Mailbox cleanup' in Outlook.
Raise a ticket to request a quota increase.

title: Suspicious or phishing email received
steps: Do not click links or open attachments.
Report it using the 'Report phishing' button or forward it to the security team.
If you clicked a link or entered a password, change your password immediately.
Raise a high priority ticket so Security can check your account.

title: LAN cable connection not working
steps: Check that the cable is firmly connected at both ends.
Try a different cable or wall port.
Disable and enable the Ethernet adapter.
Update the network adapter driver.
Run Network Troubleshooter from settings.

title: Cannot access shared folder or network drive
steps: Check that you are on the office network or VPN.
Reconnect the mapped drive using the full path.
Check that your account has permission to the folder.
Restart the computer and try again.
Raise a ticket mentioning the exact folder path.

title: Website blocked by company
steps: Check that the URL is spelled correctly.
Websites may be blocked by company policy.
If you need it for work, raise a ticket with the URL and business reason.
Do not try to bypass the proxy or firewall.

title: Microphone not working in meetings
steps: Check that you are not muted in the meeting and on the keyboard.
Select the correct microphone in the meeting app settings.
Allow microphone access in Windows privacy settings.
Unplug and replug the headset.
Restart the meeting app.

title: Camera not working
steps: Check for a physical camera shutter or Fn key.
Close other apps that may be using the camera.
Allow camera access in Windows privacy settings.
Select the correct camera in the meeting app.
Update or reinstall the camera driver.

title: Teams or Zoom lag, poor video quality
steps: Close other apps and tabs.
Turn off your video temporarily to save bandwidth.
Move closer to the router or use a wired connection.
Update the meeting app.
Run a speed test and make sure you have at least 5 Mbps.

title: Virus or malware suspected
steps: Disconnect from the network.
Run a full antivirus scan.
Do not enter passwords on this device until it is clean.
Uninstall unknown programs.
Raise a high priority ticket so Security can check the device.

title: Lost or stolen company laptop or phone
steps: Report it to the IT and Security team immediately.
Change your passwords from another device.
The admin can remotely lock or wipe the device.
Report to the police if it was stolen and share the copy with IT.

title: Need access or permission to a system
steps: Confirm the exact system or folder name you need.
Get your manager's approval.
Raise an access request ticket with the approval attached.
Wait for confirmation from the system owner; this may take 1 to 2 working days.
